text:
Maya: quick sync — we need to finalize SDK defaults for retries + pagination across Python/TS/Go. trying to avoid per-language divergence. thoughts?
Chris: what's the absolute must-have constraints? latency-sensitive hosted API, but also Dedicated/private where retries can be harmful if server-side is overloaded.
Samir: proposal: 1) automatic retries only for idempotent unary calls (get/model-metadata/embeddings) 2) paginated list endpoints: expose both page-level and item-level iterators, but default to a zero-surprise `items()` iterator in py/ts that hides pages. 3) streaming/generator endpoints should never retry mid-stream without explicit resume token semantics.
Priya: +1. add: SDK should expose the RetryPolicy as a first-class config object (backoff, retryable codes, max attempts) and we should wire it consistently to transport adapters. that way teams can opt-out per-call.
Kevin: default backoff we use elsewhere: exponential base=100ms, multiplier=2, jitter=0.15, max=4s, max_attempts=5. recommend keeping that as SDK default but documented as conservative for latency-sensitive routes.
Chris: for pagination ergonomics across languages: python iterate -> `for item in client.list_models(...).items():` typescript: `for await (const item of client.listModels().items())` go: return `Iterator` that has `Next() (Item, error)` and `ResumeToken()`. important: resume token visible in Go for server-side checkpoints.
Samir: on transport shape: keep a thin abstraction: unary(request) -> response, and stream(request) -> AsyncIterable<ResponseChunk>. transports can implement both (http/htt2/grpc). the SDK layer should not care about protocol, only about "is_streaming" and "supports_resume_tokens" capability flags.
Maya: what about client-side prefetching? i.e., prefetch N pages to hide latency but increases request load. should that live in the SDK or be an opt-in helper?
Priya: opt-in helper. default = no prefetch. add a `prefetch_pages` option on the iterator builder and a safety valve in console (observability to show prefetch cost).
Kevin: edge case: failed retry of a page that changed size (server-side) — we need to guarantee item-level idempotency. easiest is to surface page cursors as opaque tokens and treat resume tokens as authoritative: if resume token doesn't match expected position, return RetryNotSafe.
Chris: propose concrete python surface snippet to align languages:
```python
client = RedwoodClient(retry_policy=RetryPolicy.default())
for item in client.list_documents(project_id).items(prefetch_pages=0):
    do_work(item)
```
And a streaming example where resume is explicit:
```python
stream = client.stream_logs(resume_token="abc")
for chunk in stream:
    process(chunk)
# no auto-retry unless resume_token passed in constructor
```
Samir: small note: make default retryable error mapping: 429, 503 -> retryable; 500 -> not retryable by default unless endpoint marked idempotent. keep mapping configurable.
Maya: action items: 1) eng-platform owners (Samir/Chris) draft an RFC for transport capability flags + RetryPolicy schema, 2) SDK owners add iterator helpers with `items()` + `pages()` and `prefetch_pages` opt-in, 3) docs: concrete examples for py/ts/go and migration guidance.
Chris: filing RFC now — will link PR.
ci-bot: New RFC draft created: https://redwood.internal/rfc/1234 (draft) — comments welcome :eyes:
Maya: thanks — can we include a small test harness to validate behavior across our hosted/dedicated/private modes? integration tests should simulate throttling 429 and mid-page failures.
Priya: I'll add a test plan section to the RFC.
Kevin: also add a note about telemetry: expose retry counts per-call and pages fetched to Console for cost visibility.
Maya: perfect. wrapping up — we'll review RFC Monday and aim to land SDK helpers in the next sprint. :thumbsup:
